title: Analysing Clinical Survival Data with OptSurvCutR
text: clinical research, continuous biomarkers often simplified binary groups using arbitrary thresholds like median splits. convenient, approach obscures meaningful biological structure. OptSurvCutR package built specifically discover true, mathematically optimal thresholds. core powerhouse Genetic Algorithm—evolutionary search engine capable navigating massive, multi-dimensional data find optimal cut-points simultaneously, task traditional methods freeze. Furthermore, package features built-statistical safety nets, including 2-Tier Schoenfeld diagnostic check comprehensive 4-Tier Validation Stability system. Crucially, engine allows covariate adjustment, ensuring discovered biomarker thresholds provide independent prognostic value even controlling established clinical confounders like age disease staging. vignette, apply workflow classic Mayo Clinic Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) dataset evaluate raw serum bilirubin, controlling age edema.

what: 🔍 Automated Performance Grading: The 4-Tier Stability Assessment
title: Analysing Clinical Survival Data with OptSurvCutR
text: Following bootstrap calculations, OptSurvCutR evaluates Precision (Confidence Interval width relative overall data range) Validity (absence interval overlap), grading model health four distinct tiers: Tier 1 (OPTIMAL): Narrow intervals (CI Width < 30%) paired complete cohort separation. Tier 2 (DISTINCT): Zero overlap confidence zones regardless width. Thresholds may float slightly, risk boundaries remain clear. Tier 3 (CAUTION): Moderate parameter variance (CI Width 30%–60%) accompanied overlapping intervals. Tier 4 (UNSTABLE): High variance (CI Width > 60%) overlapping intervals, signaling severe data -fitting. precise documentation, compile numerical confidence intervals directly clean markdown summary table. Covariate-Adjusted Stability Intervals Bilirubin Risk Thresholds see thresholds remain tightly anchored scatter across iterations, inspect bootstrap density landscape.

what: Example: Quick Workflow with Simulated Cohort Data
title: Optimal Survival Cut-Point Discovery for Time-to-Event Analysis
code: library(OptSurvCutR) library(survival) library(dplyr)  # Generate a reproducible, synthetic survival dataset set.seed(123) n <- 200 crc <- tibble(   abundance = rnorm(n, mean = 5, sd = 2),   age = rnorm(n, mean = 60, sd = 10),   # Generate survival times influenced by biomarker abundance   time = rexp(n, rate = 0.05 * exp(0.3 * (abundance > 5.5) + 0.02 * age)),   event = sample(c(0, 1), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)) ) %>% filter(time > 0)  # Step 1: Determine the optimal number of cut-points num_res <- find_cutpoint_number(   data = crc, predictor = "abundance",   outcome_time = "time", outcome_event = "event",   method = "genetic", criterion = "BIC",   max_cuts = 3, nmin = 0.25, seed = 123 ) summary(num_res)  # Step 2: Find the precise cut-point locations cut_res <- find_cutpoint(   data = crc, predictor = "abundance",   outcome_time = "time", outcome_event = "event",   method = "genetic", criterion = "logrank",   num_cuts = num_res$optimal_num_cuts,  # Dynamically pass the result from Step 1   nmin = 0.275,                         # Fine-tuned for stability   n_perm = 50, n_cores = 2, seed = 123 ) summary(cut_res)  # Automatically reports Hazard Ratios & Schoenfeld Diagnostics!  # Step 3: Validate stability with bootstrap val_res <- validate_cutpoint(   cutpoint_result = cut_res,   num_replicates = 150, n_cores = 2, seed = 123 ) summary(val_res)  # Automatically grades threshold stability (Tiers 1-4)!  # Step 4: Visualise outcomes via atomic native plots plot(cut_res, type = "distribution")   # Continuous Predictor Density Split Map plot(cut_res, type = "outcome")        # Premium Custom Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves plot(cut_res, type = "forest")         # Hazard Ratio Forest Plot with Cohort Sample Sizes plot(cut_res, type = "diagnostic")     # Schoenfeld Residual Proportional Hazards Check plot_validation(val_res, focus_cuts = c(1, 2)) # 2D Contour Elevation Stability Topology
